newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau casino police chief wounded in attack.
newsitem.headline: Macau casino police chief wounded in attack.

text.p: Macau's chief casino police official has been seriously wounded by a gunman on a motorcycle in the Portuguese-ruled territory, police said on Wednesday.
Lieutenant-Colonel Manuel Antonio Apolinario was hit by two bullets, one in the face and one in the neck, and was under police guard in hospital, they said.
The assailant rode up and shot Apolinario on Tuesday night as he climbed into his car on the Avenida da Praia Grande, the centre of the tiny enclave's bustling casino tourism industry.
Apolinario was in charge of policing Macau's casinos, and was a former chief of police intelligence in the territory.
Police sources, speaking anonymously, said the assassination attempt may have been a revenge attack by Chinese triad gangsters involved in illicit casino-related business.
Macau has been rocked by a string of gang killings in recent months, but Apolinario was the highest ranking colonial official to have been attacked.
Portugal is to hand Macau back to China in 1999, ending more than four centuries of colonial administration.

The run-up to the handover has been marked by smooth ties with Beijing, but also a rise in the activities of Chinese triad crime gangs competing for control of gambling-related businesses such as loan-sharking and protection rackets, the sources said.
